cars.variant: D-500 single-carb 315 Hemi two-door hardtop — 1956 USA revised AMA, PowerFlite
cars.specification_market: 1956 USA D-500 two-door hardtop with single four-barrel 315 Hemi and selected PowerFlite automatic, using Dodge’s AMA sheets revised 15 February 1956. Count the original 1955–1956-body Dodge performance-road family once across Coronet/Royal/Custom Royal trim, roofs and package alternatives. Not the 1953 pace-car replica, D-500-1 racer, later D-501 or late-1960s Coronet Super Bee. Retain advertised engine brake horsepower and factory test convention in native units. No road-test acceleration, dyno wheel power, adjusted shift points, universal race availability, hardtop dimensions from default sedan tables or curb mass inferred.
cars.summary: The original D-500 is a landmark early Dodge performance-road programme, combining a hemispherical-head V8 with upgraded chassis and brakes. Racer Brown’s contemporary 1,300-mile evaluation documents its unusually complete performance, handling and stopping ability while explicitly distinguishing the road car from the D-500-1 competition package.

sources.publisher: Dodge Division, Chrysler Corporation / Over-Drive facsimile
sources.title: 1956 Dodge AMA Consolidated Specification Questionnaire — revised 15 February 1956
sources.source_type: Original manufacturer AMA specification sheets, hosted scan
sources.notes: 25-page scan, 10,652,364 bytes. Full indexes 0, 1, 3, 5, 12, 13, 14 and 18 visually read. D-500 columns and package footnotes kept separate. Sheet 2 confirms 9.25:1 and advertised 260 bhp/330 lb-ft, with its stated SAE Engine Test Code accessories convention; no modern net conversion. Sheet 6 identifies one Carter WCFB-2443-SA versus D-500-1 dual carburettors. Sheets 13–15 establish PowerFlite, converter, wheels and 12-inch brakes; 19 identifies the D-500 two-door hardtop. Default sedan dimensions and shipping weights are not imported.

sources.title: Dodge D-500 — Racer Brown, May 1956
sources.source_type: Contemporary first-hand road test, publisher archive
sources.notes: Original May 1956 test republished January 2023. Admission evidence: 1,300-plus-mile road evaluation with strong handling and braking results, clearly separating street D-500 from competition D-500-1. Initial compression figure conflicts with later text and factory 9.25:1; use factory sheets. No test-specific tuned shifts, performance times, speculative race outputs or standard-equipment claims imported.

facts.title: Why this car belongs
facts.explanation: The original D-500 is a landmark early Dodge performance-road programme, combining a hemispherical-head V8 with upgraded chassis and brakes. Racer Brown’s contemporary 1,300-mile evaluation documents its unusually complete performance, handling and stopping ability while explicitly distinguishing the road car from the D-500-1 competition package.

media.caption: 1956 Custom Royal Lancer D500 photographed by Greg Gjerdingen at Midwest Mopars in the Park, Farmington, Minnesota, June 2013. Representative two-door hardtop body and D500-style crossed-flag identification; trim shown is Custom Royal. The photograph does not authenticate engine internals, carburetion, transmission, braking equipment, package identity or restoration originality.
